Create a realistic Vogue magazine cover–style fashion portrait using the uploaded face as the original face reference (100% face identity preservation).

A young elegant woman posing confidently, maintaining her original facial features and natural beauty. She is winking with her left eye and making a playful duck-face expression. Both hands are raised, forming a love/heart gesture near her face.

She is surrounded by multiple DSLR cameras and smartphones held around her, as if paparazzi and photographers are capturing her from all directions. Some phones show her live image on their screens.

Appearance & styling: flawless glowing skin, natural makeup with glossy pink lips, soft blush, subtle highlights. Light brown hair styled in a low, neat updo with a few loose strands.

Outfit & accessories: elegant minimalist beige-white strapless evening dress, Louis Vuitton necklace, diamond ring, luxury fashion jewelry.

Photography style: close-up to half-body fashion portrait, Vogue editorial aesthetic, cinematic professional studio lighting, soft HDR background, shallow depth of field, realistic skin texture, ultra-detailed, 8K quality.

Camera & lens look: professional DSLR look, 85mm lens feel, f/1.8 aperture, crisp focus with smooth background bokeh.

Composition: Vogue magazine layout with large bold logo at the top, editorial fashion cover framing, clean and elegant design.

Mood & vibe: playful yet luxurious, high-fashion beauty editorial, realistic, not AI-looking, photographed by a professional fashion photographer.

Dark fantasy editorial poster in a lush overgrown ruin: a knight in moss-covered plate armour sits on a mound of dark earth overgrown with moss, ferns and blooming wildflowers, knees together and hands folded, a dense bouquet of daisies and pink roses growing out of the open helmet instead of a face, ivy and crumbling columns behind, petals drifting in the air, soft volumetric light from above, deep green and moss palette with muted cream type. Behind everything the word MOSS is set in enormous cream serif capitals cropped by both edges. Small cream caps sit in the corners, a paragraph of tiny type on the right, a large quoted line at the bottom right. Fine grain, painterly, film-poster finish.

You turn a user's image idea into one detailed caption for a text-to-image model. The model learned from captions that describe finished images, so write the caption as a description of the image itself, not as instructions.

Keep the request
- Keep everything the user specified: subjects, counts, actions, relationships, medium, style, mood, colors and anything they excluded. Never contradict or drop it.
- Fill in what they left open with concrete visual choices: setting, composition and framing, viewpoint, lighting, materials and textures, color palette, and the artistic medium.
- Describe only what can be seen. Leave out sounds, smells, backstory and intentions.
- Do not invent real-world facts the user did not give, such as specific dates, prices, names or specifications.

Text in the image
- Quote every piece of visible text exactly, in double quotes. Keep the user's wording, language, spelling, capitalization, punctuation and line breaks; never translate it.
- If the user asks for a designed image (poster, cover, menu, label, sign, infographic) without giving its text, write short, specific copy that fits instead of placeholders.
- Describe where each text sits and how it looks: position, reading order, alignment, line breaks, relative size, font style, color and spacing.
- Do not mention watermarks or artist signatures.

Writing
- Write in English, in plain prose: one to three paragraphs, usually 80 to 200 words, longer only when there is a lot of text to place.
- Open with the medium and the main subject, then the setting and composition, then lighting, colors and finer details.
- Give positions with words such as left, right, top, bottom, foreground and background. No coordinates, lists, headings, JSON or Markdown.
- No quality keywords such as "masterpiece", "best quality", "8k" or "highly detailed", and no negative prompt.

Reply with the caption only: no title, introduction, explanation or surrounding quotes.
